# PAA Python Phase Ordered Progress Tree

## Purpose

This is the progress tree for building the Python PAA system in the correct dependency order.

It is phase-ordered on purpose.
We should use it to track where we are and what can be built next without breaking the North Star structure.

## Status Legend

- `[complete]` implemented and documented strongly enough to build on
- `[active]` current build focus
- `[pending]` required next but not built yet
- `[deferred]` intentionally postponed
- `[transitional]` still present in code but not part of the final ownership model

## Phase Ordered Tree

```text
Phase 0. Governing Truth Lock [complete]
├── Python realization profile [complete]
├── language-profile terminology framework [complete]
├── methodology workflow note [complete]
├── node dependency review [complete]
├── target structure diagram [complete]
└── build sequence from structure [complete]

Phase 1. North Star Alignment [complete]
├── North Star architecture doc [complete]
├── final target structure agreed [complete]
├── simplified layer rule agreed [complete]
│   └── cli -> api -> services/app logic -> data layer [complete]
└── MethodologyExecution pointer made explicit [complete]

Phase 2. Data Layer Foundation [active]
├── repositories/component_design review [complete]
├── realization type operations normalized [complete]
├── element-realization mapping operations normalized [complete]
├── repositories/methodology_execution review [pending]
├── pointer persistence coverage checked [pending]
└── db.py responsibility inventory for this slice [complete]

Phase 3. Services/App Logic Over Data [pending]
├── application DTOs for taxonomy operations [complete]
├── application services for taxonomy operations [complete]
├── methodology pointer app-service operations [pending]
└── pointer-aware command validation where needed [pending]

Phase 4. API Exposure [pending]
├── realization type routes [complete]
├── element-realization mapping routes [complete]
├── methodology execution routes [pending]
└── composition cleanup with Dishka if needed [pending]

Phase 5. CLI Proof Surface [pending]
├── paa commands for realization types [complete]
├── paa commands for realization mappings [complete]
├── pointer inspection/preflight command path [pending]
└── integration proof through paa [complete]

Phase 6. db.py Extraction By Destination [deferred]
├── extract one coherent responsibility cluster [pending]
├── move to repositories or low-level data support [pending]
├── prove through paa after each extraction [pending]
└── repeat until db.py is no longer a dumping ground [pending]

Phase 7. Runtime And Producer Continuation [pending]
├── continue producer work on the same stack [pending]
├── continue runtime work on the same stack [pending]
├── keep pointer-governed transitions real [pending]
└── keep CLI proof as the main validation path [pending]
```

## Current Pointer To Where We Are

The current system position is:
- Phase 2. Data Layer Foundation `[active]`
- Active slice: `S03` Methodology Pointer Inspection And Transition
- Completed layer for active slice: not started
- Next layer for active slice: data layer

That means:
- the design and planning frame is ready
- the repository normalization for realization-type registry and mapping support is in place
- the `component_taxonomy` app surface now covers both realization types and element-realization mappings
- the runtime API now exposes both realization types and element-realization mappings
- `paa` now exposes and proves both realization types and element-realization mappings end to end
- the next correct work is `S03` data-layer work for methodology pointer inspection and transition
- this is still not the time to start cutting random pieces out of `db.py`

## Build Order Rule

Only move down the tree.
Do not skip upward dependencies.

That means:
1. data layer before new service behavior
2. services/app logic before API expansion
3. API before CLI proof surface for the new command family
4. CLI proof before `db.py` extraction for that responsibility cluster

## Methodology Pointer Rule

At every phase after Phase 1, ask:
- where is pointer truth persisted
- how is pointer truth read
- how is pointer truth advanced
- how is pointer truth exposed through `paa`

If a build slice cannot answer those questions clearly, it is probably not aligned yet.

## Phase Exit Rules

### Exit Phase 2 when:
- repository-backed taxonomy operations are real
- repository-backed methodology pointer operations are confirmed for the slice
- the first `db.py` destination cluster is identified clearly

### Exit Phase 3 when:
- application DTOs and services are in place for the first taxonomy flow
- pointer-aware service behavior exists where required

### Exit Phase 4 when:
- the API exposes the same operations without owning business logic

### Exit Phase 5 when:
- `paa` can perform and prove the real operations through the system path

### Enter Phase 6 only when:
- the destination structure for the `db.py` cluster already exists
- the relevant `paa` proof path is already real

## Usage Rule

Use this tree as the progress tracker for implementation planning.

When we start a slice:
1. mark the active phase explicitly if it changed
2. record the active slice id from the build map
3. record the exact subtree items expected to move

When we complete a slice:
1. update the phase status if the phase exit rule was satisfied
2. mark the exact subtree item that moved
3. mark the completed slice id from the build map
4. keep the next active item explicit

That way the tree stays honest and we always know where we are.
